question: Does a second clean builder produce the same dist/ and the same tarball as the candidate?

method.source: git archive HEAD | tar -x -C <copy> for each copy
method.isolation: Each copy got its own HOME, npm_config_cache, and TMPDIR under its own directory.
method.comparison: dist/index.js SHA-256, sorted dist/ path+hash digest, tarball SHA-256, file counts

finding.reading: Two independent clean copies, each with a fresh HOME and cache, produced byte-identical tarballs. This is stronger than the B2 content-identical case: no mtime normalization was needed.

result: B1: dist and tarball both match. O34 B, strongest wording. O43 A not triggered.
limits: Both builders ran on the same machine and toolchain; this is not a cross-machine reproducibility claim.
The tarball contains only dist, README, LICENSE, CREDITS, and CHANGELOG; docs/ and scripts/ are not packaged.
No publish, stage, tag, or approval was performed.
